method.tab_policy: Used NEW tabs inside the browser's existing default browsing context (sharing storage/cache, not a new incognito-style BrowserContext). Reason: browser.new_context() pages were torn down by Chrome when the creating Playwright process disconnected, which would have discarded in-progress state between tool calls; plain new_page() in the default context survives disconnects. The 2 pre-existing 'TRACE-RPG: The Sealed Lighthouse' tabs and the original about:blank tab were never closed or navigated.
method.console_page_error_capture: page.on('console'/'pageerror'/'requestfailed'/'response') listeners were attached immediately after each new page was created, before any navigation, on every one of the 4 page/viewport passes.

operational_finding_blocking_issue_and_f.finding: At task start, the project's static file server (python3 -m http.server 8877 --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory game-track/web, PID 30420) was unresponsive to ALL clients: curl, Python http.client, and the pre-provisioned real headless Chrome browser itself (page.goto -> net::ERR_EMPTY_RESPONSE) on every path including '/'. Confirmed via lsof that only the browser's own 2 already-open tabs held established keep-alive connections to it; no other client could get a response (immediate empty reply, not a hang).
operational_finding_blocking_issue_and_f.action_taken: Restarted the identical, unmodified command (python3 -m http.server 8877 --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory game-track/web) after stopping the unresponsive PID. This is the plain stdlib static file server (no app code, no GDScript, no test hooks) and matches the prior session's own convention recorded in this repo at qa/npc-panel-html-2026-10-15/cleanup.json, where the same server was explicitly described as harness-managed and expected to be started/stopped per QA session. No game source, build output, or test hook was touched.
operational_finding_blocking_issue_and_f.verification_after_restart: curl 200 on /, /public/, /dashboard/, and /public/index.pck (exact 13,401,824-byte size match); the real browser's page.goto then succeeded cleanly on every subsequent pass.
operational_finding_blocking_issue_and_f.disclosure: Reporting this prominently and transparently as requested ('If real UI blocker, report exact steps'); this was an infrastructure/serving-process issue, not a defect in the rebuilt game assets themselves, which were verified byte-identical (see asset_sha256 below) before and after the restart.

pointer_release_Esc.status: PASS for the core mechanic (Esc does toggle real document.pointerLockElement state, confirmed twice) with ONE precise unverified boundary flagged below.
pointer_release_Esc.unverified_boundary: On the second Escape toggle, fired only ~400ms after the first, document.pointerLockElement read non-null while the in-game HUD label still showed the released-state text. Chromium is documented to throttle/cooldown rapid requestPointerLock() re-entry (~1.25s) after an exit; this mismatch may be a benign artifact of re-toggling faster than that cooldown, or a genuine HUD-label lag. It was not re-verified with a longer interval in this pass, so it is reported as an open, unverified observation rather than a confirmed defect. This is additional, narrower evidence alongside this repo's existing DEF-010 (defect-register.md), which separately found headless automation historically did not reliably obtain real pointer lock at all; this session's browser (launched with --disable-blink-features=AutomationControlled) DID obtain real pointer-lock grants on 3 of 4 checks, which is new information worth recording without re-closing or contradicting DEF-010's own test conditions.
